t:
That 

    (a) 
the article description of item 807.00 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States is amended by striking out the comma after “exported” in clause (a) and by striking out “for the purpose of such assembly and return to the United States,”.
 
    (b) 
The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the date of the enactment of this Act. Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 120th day after the date of the enactment of this Act, the entry or withdrawal of any article—

        (1) 
which was made after August 30, 1963, and before the date of the enactment of this Act, and
 
        (2) 
with respect to which the amount of duty would be smaller if the amendments made by subsection (a) applied to such entry or withdrawal,
   shall, notwithstanding the provisions of section 514 of the Tariff Act of 1930 or any other provision of law, be liquidated or reliquidated as though such entry or withdrawal had been made on the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an importer's "request" filed with a customs officer is an outside party taking part in a federal decision. It is really an application for a benefit (reliquidation of duties at a lower rate), which the definition excludes from participation. The rest of the section only amends a tariff schedule description and involves no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 120th day after the date of the enactment of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section amends the text of the Tariff Schedules and establishes the effective date and liquidation rules for customs entries. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The mention of 'Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer' refers to a procedural mechanism for applying the new law to past entries, not a participatory process in making the decision.
qwen_block.s: That (a) the article description of item 807.00 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States is amended by striking out the comma after “exported” in clause (a) and by striking out “for the purpose of such assembly and return to the United States,”.

opus.w: The only outside-party involvement is an importer asking for its own past entries to be reliquidated at the lower duty. That is like applying for a benefit or refund, which the definition excludes, and it is not input on a federal policy decision. Nothing else in the section creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside groups, or a right to sue.
opus.s: Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 120th day after the date of the enactment of this Act, the entry or withdrawal of any article
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Subsection (b) lets an outside party, the importer, file "request therefor... with the customs officer concerned," and that request leads to a federal action (liquidating or reliquidating the entry). An outside party starting a federal decision can look like participation. That reading fails. The request is a claim for the importer's own refund of duty, which is like applying for a benefit, and the definition excludes that. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or new right to sue. Subsection (a) is just a technical amendment to the tariff wording.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes a procedural mechanism for importers to request retroactive application of a tariff amendment to specific entries. This is analogous to filing a claim or application for a specific financial adjustment, which falls under the exclusion for 'applications for benefits or grants.' It does not involve consultation, public comment, or advisory input into a broader federal decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 120th day after the date of the enactment of this Act, the entry or withdrawal of any article... shall... be liquidated or reliquidated as though such entry or withdrawal had been made on the date of the enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "request" filed by an importer constitutes participation because it involves an outside party interacting with a federal official (the customs officer) to influence a decision (liquidation of duty). However, this is a procedural mechanism for applying a retroactive statutory amendment to a specific transaction, akin to filing a claim or application for a benefit/refund, rather than a process for public input into policy-making or rulemaking. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants," and this request is essentially an application for the retroactive application of a tariff change to a specific entry. Furthermore, there is no consultation, hearing, or advisory role involved; it is a unilateral request processed according to fixed statutory criteria.
